intro: Big climbs are team efforts. These are some that worked, and what each one teaches.

stories.title: The first ascent of Everest
stories.org: British Everest Expedition, led by John Hunt
stories.text: A big team of climbers, Sherpa and porters set up a chain of camps. Hunt chose two summit pairs. The first pair turned back, exhausted. On 29 May Hillary and Tenzing reached the top and spent about fifteen minutes there.
stories.lesson: Preparation and teamwork put two people on the summit. Everyone on that expedition had a part in it.

stories.title: Stopping short on Kangchenjunga
stories.org: British Kangchenjunga Expedition, led by Charles Evans
stories.text: Joe Brown and George Band climbed to within a few steps of the summit and stopped. They had promised the Sikkimese that they would not set foot on the top, which the local people hold sacred. The tradition of leaving the final few metres has been kept by many climbers since.
stories.lesson: Respect for local belief is part of the job. It also shows that a summit is not the only measure of a climb.

stories.title: Junko Tabei on Everest
stories.text: An avalanche buried Tabei at Camp II on 4 May. Sherpa guides dug her out. Twelve days later, on 16 May, she walked to the top, the first woman to stand on Everest.
stories.lesson: Good teams look after each other, and a bad day does not have to end an expedition.

stories.title: Everest with no bottled oxygen
stories.text: Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler reached the top on 8 May. Habeler was worried that the thin air would damage his brain, so he descended very quickly. Both were fine. The climb changed what people believed was possible.
stories.lesson: Limits that experts accept as fixed sometimes turn out to be assumptions.

stories.title: Bachendri Pal, first Indian woman on Everest
stories.text: Bachendri Pal reached the summit on 23 May 1984 as part of an Indian expedition. She went on to encourage many women to take up climbing in India.
stories.lesson: One visible success can open a whole sport to people who had been left out.

stories.title: Project Possible
stories.org: Nirmal Purja and a Nepali team
stories.text: Purja climbed all fourteen 8,000 m peaks in six months and six days. The previous record was close to eight years. The climb needed support from teammates and arranged flights and permits.
stories.lesson: Logistics and planning matter as much as strength.

stories.title: K2 in winter
stories.text: K2 was the only 8,000 m peak never climbed in winter. On 16 January ten Nepali climbers took the last steps together to the top, in temperatures reported to be around minus 60 °C.
stories.lesson: Sherpa and Nepali climbers carry the work on these peaks, and this climb finally put them in front.
